sources.entry: Mac Monitor - Lightweight menu bar monitor for RAM, CPU, network and disk, focused on memory pressure. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Ahmadjondev/MacMonitor) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Mac Monitor is a lightweight macOS menu-bar system monitor showing live RAM, CPU, network and disk stats, with a focus on memory pressure and optional pressure-aware memory cleaning.
keywords: check if mac is out of memory
summary.what_it_does: Mac Monitor shows one live number in the macOS menu bar: network speed by default, or RAM % or CPU %. Clicking it opens a dashboard with memory (used, pressure level, composition, swap, pressure graph), processor (total and per-core CPU), network (speeds, totals, local IPv4), and startup-volume storage with disk throughput. The full window adds CPU breakdown, load average, process and thread counts, packet and per-interface network stats, battery details, and GPU utilization where exposed. An Insights view shows RAM and CPU history charts for the last 24 hours, saved as 1-minute aggregates. Memory cleaning runs macOS's purge on demand, or automatically only when memory pressure is critical, and it can send a notification when pressure turns critical. The app reads local macOS APIs and states that it makes no network connections.
use_cases: watch memory pressure on a Mac
see live network speed in the menu bar
monitor CPU and RAM usage at a glance
check whether a Mac is actually out of memory
free inactive memory on macOS when needed
review battery health and cycle count
find which apps use the most memory
how_to_run: Download MacMonitor.dmg from the latest release and drag Mac Monitor to Applications
Approve the unsigned app on first launch (System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway, or xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine)
git clone the repository, cd MacMonitor, then run ./build.sh
notable: Fixed-width menu bar item so neighbouring icons do not jitter
Cleans memory based on memory pressure rather than a blind timer; auto-clean only at critical pressure and off by default
No third-party dependencies and states it makes no network connections
Three interface languages (English, Russian, Uzbek) switchable live
Optional narrowly scoped sudoers rule allows passwordless purge of /usr/sbin/purge only
caveats: Release is ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so macOS blocks the first launch and requires manual approval
Silent memory cleaning needs an optional sudoers rule; without it, Clean now asks for an administrator password and auto-clean is skipped
Not distributed on the Mac App Store because the sandbox blocks its purge, ps and LaunchAgent features
Narrower hardware sensor coverage than Stats or iStat Menus (no fan speeds or many sensors)
